channel.title: Acme: Light News
channel.description: Positive, lighthearted and unusual current news.

item.title: Martin Luther King Jr.’s lost handwritten speech draft resurfaces
item.description: A heavily revised handwritten draft prepared by Martin Luther King Jr. on the morning of the March on Washington has emerged after six decades. Xernona Clayton found it in her late husband Edward Clayton’s desk in the 1990s and is auctioning it through Christie’s to benefit charities including the King Center.

item.title: Florida neighbor braves floodwater to rescue vulnerable residents
item.description: Rick Addante crossed shoulder-deep water in Palm Bay after a 1,000-year rain event to reach two vulnerable neighbors—an 80-year-old recovering from heart surgery and a wheelchair user with ALS. He helped move them to safety as Florida wildlife officers arrived with airboats, calling the effort a community-wide rescue.

item.title: Genome sequencing helps stop an infant’s 110 daily seizures
item.description: Doctors in Dubai used whole-genome sequencing to identify the rare gene variant behind infant Adnan’s seizures, which struck about every 13 minutes. A compassionate-use treatment targeting the associated ion channel stopped them, and he remained seizure-free for weeks after beginning the experimental oral medicine.

item.title: Ultrarunner becomes first woman to run 100 continuous miles in Antarctica
item.description: Canadian ultrarunner Stephanie Case became the first woman to complete 100 continuous miles in Antarctica. She covered 38 loops of a 4.2-kilometre course in 17 hours, 31 minutes and 39 seconds, finishing second overall among 28 runners in the extraordinary polar race.

item.title: Bronx Zoo gives trafficked parrots a second chance
item.description: Dozens of white-fronted Amazon parrots and orange-fronted conures seized from the illegal pet trade at the U.S.-Mexico border are recovering at the Bronx Zoo. A zoo partnership has assisted nine parrot confiscations since 2022; two rescued red-lored Amazons even raised two chicks there this summer.

item.title: Lowe’s coworkers throw their ‘store mom’ a first 100th-birthday party
item.description: After a stroke, Gretchen Sollo began walking the aisles of a Lowe’s in Bradley, Illinois, and has logged an estimated 1,500 miles there over five years. Staff adopted her as their “store mom” and gathered with family to give Sollo her first workplace birthday party as she turned 100.

item.title: Superhero window washers brighten a day at Children’s Nebraska
item.description: Young patients in Omaha looked out their hospital windows on Nov. 11 to find costumed superheroes descending the building with squeegees. The window washers’ recurring tradition turns routine exterior maintenance into a surprise visit from familiar caped figures.

item.title: Visitors overlooked 280 Ice Age engravings in a Catalan cave
item.description: Archaeologists identified horses, deer, a bear and abstract designs on walls passed by tourists for decades in Cova de la Font Major. The roughly 26,000-year-old collection is the largest known in Catalonia and the third largest from Mediterranean Iberia.

item.title: Spain’s Cantabrian brown bears double their population
item.description: Conservation measures helped the population rise from roughly 140 bears early this century to about 370, while their occupied range grew to more than 17,000 square kilometers. Researchers say management plans now need updating as the bears reclaim suitable habitat.

item.title: Kerala rescue saves more than 19,500 orchids from roadwork
item.description: Researchers moved 27,324 orchids from trees threatened by road construction in southern India to a beach and two urban wetlands. After 12 to 24 months, nearly 71% were still alive; many flowered and produced seed, turning an emergency rescue into a promising conservation model.

item.title: A shy shelter dog finds the patient home she needed
item.description: Alena, a terrier mix whose kennel anxiety discouraged adopters, found a home six days after an online feature showed her relaxed foster-care personality. Her new family had experience with timid dogs and gives her space to approach on her own terms; the shelter calls it a perfect match.

item.title: Beaver family returns to the Loch Ness watershed after 500 years
item.description: A family of six beavers was released Nov. 4 at the Dundreggan rewilding estate, the first recorded return to the Loch Ness catchment since the species was hunted to extinction in Scotland. The project plans to restore at least 15 family groups across the watershed over three years.

item.title: Rehabilitated bald eagle takes flight over North Carolina Zoo
item.description: A four-year-old female bald eagle found barely responsive at a landfill in September returned to the wild after nearly two months of care. Her Nov. 4 flight over the North Carolina Zoo's lake also marked the 25th anniversary of its wildlife rehabilitation center.

item.title: Volunteers plant nearly 500 pines in New Mexico burn scar
item.description: Volunteers, the Rocky Mountain Youth Corps and the Los Vigiles Land Grant have planted nearly 500 ponderosa pine seedlings in the Hermit's Peak-Calf Canyon burn area since October. Crews hope to put another 500 in the ground before winter.

item.title: Georgia eighth-grader wins cheer competition as a squad of one
item.description: When the rest of her squad dropped out, eighth-grader Jorgia Walls performed alone at a Georgia cheer competition. She completed the routine before hundreds of spectators and won first place, turning an unexpected setback into an exuberant solo victory.
